# SK1072 — The spread of a freshly created array is its elements

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

An array is created inside a collection expression only so that a spread element can take it apart again.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 12.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

`SK1001` introduces collection expressions; this is the cleanup that follows one. An array built at the point of a spread lives for the length of one expression and exists only to be enumerated back into the collection that is being built beside it — the allocation, the copy and the `..` are all ceremony around a list of elements that could simply have been written there. A modernization rule without its cleanup family produces churn.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
int[] codes = [.. new[] { 200, 204 }, fallback];
```

Write:

```csharp
int[] codes = [200, 204, fallback];
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The array's element type and the outer collection's element type must be the same symbol, and that is not fussiness about a widening nobody would notice.** Before the rewrite each element is converted twice — to the array's element type, and from there to the outer collection's; after it, once. Two conversions in sequence are not the same as the one that would replace them: `new long[] { anInt }` spread into a `double[]` goes `int → long → double` and would go `int → double`, and where a user-defined conversion is on either leg the single step does not exist at all, because C# never chains two of them — so the fix would not even compile. Requiring the two element types to be equal makes both sides one conversion and removes the question. Where the outer collection's element type cannot be determined — a type implementing `IEnumerable<T>` twice, a builder-attributed target — the rule declines. ⚠ Only an array creation carrying a written initializer is matched: `new T[] { … }` and `new[] { … }`, single-dimension, at least one element, no `{ k, v }` pair among them. A nested collection expression as the spread operand has no type of its own to compare against, and a spread of anything that was not created on the spot is a spread of something the program can still see. ⚠ An **empty** creation is deliberately not matched. `[.. new T[0], a]` is `[a]`, which deletes a separator as well as an element; the empty-collection concept is `SK1073`'s and `CA1825`'s. ⚠ The elements are carried across as source text rather than rebuilt from syntax, so a comment or an alignment between them survives; the text on either side of them, which the fix deletes, is checked for a comment or a directive first. ⚠ Four further inspections in this ReSharper family are not covered: `AppendToCollectionExpression`, the two `UseArrayCreationExpression` forms and `RedundantArrayCreationExpression` outside a spread.
